extraction.Name: John Lamont
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment, when it was issued, September 29, 1919, for he did not want to pay the taxes; that the Indian Agency advised him that, if he did not accept it, and pay the taxes, that the land would be assessed for taxes, for which it would finally be sold, so he took the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1920, he sold his allotment to Spurgeon Wadell, of Martin, South Dakota, for $1100.00 in cash, and about 12 or 14 head of steers, valued at $42.00 each, making him around $1600.00 for his land
extraction.Buyer: Spurgeon Wadell, of Martin, South Dakota, for $1100.00 in cash and about 12 or 14 head of steers valued at $42.00 each, making around $1600.00 total
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: did not sell his land for debts incurred prior to the receipt of the his patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms his wife's allotment, and works for other farmers, for his living, and that this is his only source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has fair health; has a wife and six children to support, all of whom have good health; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; allotment was 160 acres; document sworn December 22, 1928, in Shannon County, South Dakota
